instruction: nx.approximation.min_weighted_dominating_set(G, weight=None) uses the wrong cost in its greedy step. The greedy algorithm repeatedly adds the node whose weight (the node attribute named by weight, 1 if missing or weight is None) divided by the number of not-yet-dominated nodes in its closed neighborhood is smallest, until every node is dominated (in the set or adjacent to it). The current code divides by the number of closed-neighborhood nodes not in the set, so it counts nodes that a neighbor in the set already dominates and picks too many nodes. Fix the cost; a node that would dominate nothing new must never be chosen, and ties go to the earliest node in G's node order. For K5 (nodes 0-4) plus the path 4-5-6 the result must be a dominating set of 2 nodes, and for nx.Graph([(0, 1), (0, 4), (1, 4), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (2, 5)]) it is {1, 2} (it used to be {1, 2, 4}).
